21 22 StarNet is a local-first desktop harness where you create AI agents, organize them into a 23 pixel-art space station, and watch them perform real work with real models and tools. The 24 station is not decoration — it is a projection of live runtime state, and the product contract 25 is literal: **A room is a capability-scoped team**, **a hallway is** an authorized handoff 26 lane, and **a placed object is a real capability grant**. 27 The layout you draw *is* the workflow the agents run. 28 29 Start with one agent, then place bays or summon specialists to run **more, concurrently** — 30 each a **genuinely distinct, bounded agent run** with its own workspace and permissions. 31 The harness performs **real model calls, real tools, real cost** rather than animating a 32 simulation. 33 34 ## Features 35 36 | | | 37 | --- | --- | 38 | **A crew, not a chatbot** | Create agents with distinct classes, personas, and loadouts. Run several at once — each gets its own workspace, transcript, memory, and bounded permissions. | 39 | **Bring your own models** | Paste an OpenRouter key, or sign in with supported provider accounts (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google) — keys live in the OS keychain, never in the frontend. | 40 | **Message it from anywhere** | Wire agents to Telegram, Discord, Slack, Signal, or Matrix and talk to your station away from the desk. | 41 | **Night Shift** | Leave the station running and agents keep working inside an explicit, adjustable leash — every away-action is logged and reviewable. | 42 | **Recipes, skills, schedules** | Launch proven multi-step recipes, grant reusable skills, and put work on cron schedules with visible output. | 43 | **Asks before it guesses** | Task Briefs turn ambiguity into one concrete question with options — over any connected channel — instead of a silent wrong guess. | 44 | **Finished work has a front door** | Deliverables land in the OUTBOX as real files you open, not chat scrollback you archaeology. | 45 | **MCP connectors** | Attach Model Context Protocol servers and paste-a-key/OAuth connectors to extend what agents can touch. | 46 | **Voice** | Push-to-talk dictation in, one consistent station voice out. | 47 | **Real ledgers** | Spend, budgets, and run history persist on disk and are shown as-is. | 48 49 ## What is real 50 51 - Model calls stream through the local Node sidecar. 52 - Tools operate through explicit capability and consent checks. 53 - Agent memory, transcripts, spend records, tasks, and schedules persist on disk. 54 - Multiple agents run concurrently with separate workspaces and bounded permissions. 55 - The visual station projects the same runtime state the harness can prove. 56 57 StarNet does not simulate revenue, completed work, model activity, or spend. Its core product 58 law is that **the interface must never assert state the harness cannot prove.** 59 60 ## Download 61 62 Desktop builds are published on the 63 [StarNet releases page](https://github.com/androoAGI/starnet-releases/releases/latest). 64 65 | Platform | Asset | 66 | --- | --- | 67 | **Windows** (10/11, 64-bit) | `StarNet__x64-setup.exe` | 68 | **macOS — Apple Silicon** (M1–M4) | `StarNet__aarch64.dmg` | 69 | **macOS — Intel** | `StarNet__x64.dmg` | 70 71 > **Apple Silicon note:** use the native `aarch64` DMG. Avoid the `x64` DMG on Apple Silicon: 72 > it runs under Rosetta 2 rather than using the native architecture. 73 74 The public release train supports Windows and macOS. It refuses to stage a release unless the 75 Windows installer passes Authenticode and timestamp verification, both Mac builds pass 76 Developer ID checks and Apple notarization, and every updater artifact has a valid updater 77 signature. Those are pipeline requirements, not proof that a particular downloaded or installed 78 copy was tested on your machine; [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) explains what to verify and when to stop. 79 Linux packages are internal build artifacts only and are not a supported public release target. 80 81 > **Early release:** Windows is the most-tested desktop target. macOS has less real-world 82 > coverage. Broken? Tell us: 83 > **androo.agi@gmail.com**. 84 85 ## Run from source 86 87 Requirements: Node.js 18+ (Node.js 22 matches CI), Git. Rust and the 88 [Tauri prerequisites](https://v2.tauri.app/start/prerequisites/) only for the desktop shell. 89 90 The sidecar uses Node core modules only, so it runs without installing anything: 91 92 ```bash 93 git clone https://github.com/androoAGI/starnet.git 94 cd starnet 95 node sidecar/index.js 96 ``` 97 98 Open , then connect a provider — 99 **bring your own OpenRouter API key (BYOK)** or use a supported OAuth sign-in. Provider requests leave your machine when you run an agent; 100 station state, transcripts, memory, and ledgers stay in the local StarNet workspace unless you 101 explicitly use a network tool or connector. See [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md) for the full data map. 102 103 ### Run free with a local model 104 105 No key, no account, no bill: install [Ollama](https://ollama.com), pull a model 106 (`ollama pull llama3.1`), and pick **OLLAMA** as the provider — on the first-run brain screen, or 107 later in **SETTINGS → PROVIDERS**. StarNet talks to Ollama on `127.0.0.1:11434` and only reports 108 it ready once it can list your local models. Honest caveat: local models are smaller than the 109 cloud ones, so expect slower and rougher work on long tasks. 110 111 For desktop development: 112 113 ```bash 114 npm ci 115 npm run desktop:dev # dev shell 116 npm run desktop:build # build installers locally 117 ``` 118 119 ## Coming from OpenClaw or Hermes? 120 121 StarNet can import an existing agent: point it at your on-disk OpenClaw or Hermes home and it 122 mints a StarNet agent from the persona, instructions, memory, and model it finds. API keys 123 never transfer — you re-enter those in the KEYS tab. 124 125 ## Architecture 126 127 | Path | Responsibility | 128 | --- | --- | 129 | `frontend/` | Vanilla JavaScript station world and desktop UI. | 130 | `sidecar/` | Local Node agent runtime: providers, tools, persistence, budgets, consent. | 131 | `shared/` | Additive cross-boundary event and schema contracts. | 132 | `src-tauri/` | Rust/Tauri desktop shell and bundled runtime. | 133 | `test/` | Unit, contract, integration, and release gates. | 134 | `qa/` | Live QA receipts, journeys, findings ledger, and release-readiness authority. | 135 136 The frontend consumes real sidecar events over localhost HTTP/NDJSON and SSE. Secrets belong 137 to the local authority: 138 **Secrets are held by the sidecar / OS keychain, never in the frontend**. 139 140 Start with [docs/INDEX.md](docs/INDEX.md) for the living documentation. Older planning 141 documents remain in the repository as design history and are labeled accordingly. 142 143 ## Testing 144 145 ```bash 146 npm run test:fast # required merge gate 147 npm run test:http # live sidecar HTTP/E2E suite 148 npm test # validation + world + fast + HTTP suites 149 npm run security:secrets # full-history secret scan; requires Gitleaks in PATH 150 ``` 151 152 The release aggregate is `npm run qa:ready`. It is candidate-bound: any new commit invalidates 153 the prior READY receipt until the affected live gates are rerun. 154 155 ## Contributing and security 156 157 Contributions are welcome — read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and follow the 158 [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). 159 160 Do not report vulnerabilities in a public issue. Follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for private 161 reporting instructions. 162 163 ## License 164 165 StarNet is open source under the [MIT License](LICENSE). I read the `README.md`. Your message just said "Read", so I'm not sure what you want next. Here's a quick summary so far:

**StarNet** is a local-first desktop app where you build AI agents and arrange them in a pixel-art space station. The station is drawn from what the agents are actually doing: rooms are teams limited to certain tools, hallways are the paths work can be handed along, and objects you place are the permissions agents get. The agents make real model calls and use real tools, and the spending is real too.

- **Code layout:** `frontend/` is the station interface (plain JavaScript), `sidecar/` is the local Node program that runs the agents, `src-tauri/` is the desktop app shell, and `shared/` holds contracts both sides use.
- **Running it:** `node sidecar/index.js`, then open localhost:8787.
- **Tests:** `npm run test:fast` must pass before merging; `npm run qa:ready` is the release check.
- **Branch:** you're on `feat/harness-backend` with no uncommitted changes. The latest commits are website styling and command bridge QA records.

I also tried `docs/NEXT.md`, but at 274KB it's over the size limit for a single read, so I'd need to go through it in sections.

What would you like me to read? For example, `docs/NEXT.md` (the recent part), `docs/INDEX.md`, `CODE_MAP.md`, `docs/HARNESS_ARCHITECTURE.md`, or code tied to this branch.
